newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGB futures firm on dollar drop.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGB futures firm on dollar drop.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures scaled higher on Monday supported by the swift fall of the U.S. dollar, dealers said.
Hedge funds entered the market over the day to cover short positions in both contracts, which could fuel further gains.
"Buying was driven mostly by the dollar's collapse, which triggered short covering in JGB's, spilling into Euroyen," a U.S. commission house dealer said.
Weaker Tokyo stocks, pressured by the dollar, also boosted gains in euroyen futures, dealers said.
September JGBs settled at 123.25, sharply above Friday's close at 122.92 but on a small volume of 261 lots.
In Asian forex markets, the dollar struck fresh lows at 111.80 against the yen, its lowest level since November 25.
Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka's call for stability in currency rates later helped to revive the dollar from its lows, but dealers said it continued to be on the defensive.
This could provide more momentum for euroyen to attempt for new levels of resistance.
December Euroyen was at 98.95 at 1125 GMT, up from its IMM close at 98.92, and March was at 98.69 compared with 98.65.
The next level of technical resistance for December was seen at 99.00, and after that, 99.04-06.
Eurodollar futures steadied in late action after drifting down early on a bearish dollar.
The market also eased on perceptions of a smaller possibility of a U.S. interest rate hike due to last week's jobs data.
U.S. non-farm payrolls for May showed a rise of 138,000, less than economists' forecasts of a rise of more than 200,000.
December Eurodollars recovered from intraday lows to 93.84 against their IMM close at 93.86.
